### Browser tools on chat sessions

> [!NOTE]
>
> Hosted browser availability depends on t
he account and deployment. The browser workspace must be enabled to open the live pane in the Playground.\n\n`POST /chat-sessions/
messages` accepts an optional `browser: { policy?, profileId? }`. Attach it on every turn that should browse. The initial grant an
d profile are fixed; the current host policy and pinned read-only mode can narrow the effective permissions. Responses and traces
include the read-only `chatSessionId`, browser metadata, and screenshot URLs without inline image data.\n\n| Method | Path | Purpo
se |\n| - | - | - |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/browser` | Create an empty API session and its browser with `projectId`, `policy`, o
ptional `profileId`, and a stable `idempotencyKey`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/open` | Open or wake the sessi
on browser. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/command` | Execute a browser command under the session policy with a s
table `commandId`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/note` | Append a command-ledger note. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessio
ns/{sessionId}/browser/trace` | Read command receipts and screenshot evidence. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/art
ifact` | Resolve a command screenshot URL. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/close` | Release the session desktop. |
\n\nOnly the owning user can drive an API session's browser. All inputs use the public `sessionId`; conversation and browser ident
ifiers in responses are informational. Capacity refusals before execution release the turn lease so the same idempotency key can b

e retried. An execution with an unknown outcome must be inspected before attempting a new action.

iption\": \"The user behind the API key (keys act as their creator, scoped to one organization).\",\n \"responses\": {\n \"200\
the pre-run disclosure for a suite launch plan\",\n \"description\": \"What happens to a run's content BEFORE you launch it: whic
h models it calls and where they route, which LLM analyzers/judges can fire and where their evidence goes, capture/retention/regio
n facts, and the subprocessors engaged. Read-only \\u2014 never launches or gates a run. Keyed by the SAME destination-affecting s
ubset a launch selects (`caseIds`/`environmentId`/`environmentIds`); pass the selectors you would pass to a run so what this discl
oses is what that run would do. `run_eval_suite` already fetches this itself and returns it on the receipt's `disclosure` field \\
u2014 call this route directly when you need the disclosure BEFORE deciding to launch. A deployment that predates this contract an
swers 422 `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` with `details.reason: \\\"contract_unavailable\\\"`, never a partial payload \\u2014 this is a G
UARANTEE only when the deployment's missing-function error reaches this route unredacted. Production Convex can redact that same f
ailure to a generic \\\"Server Error\\\" indistinguishable from a genuine handler crash on a suite the caller CAN see; this route
has no independent way to tell the two apart in that one case, so it answers 502 instead of guessing 422 \\u2014 a caller cannot r
ely on this code alone to detect an old production deployment, and a 502 does not imply the contract is available either. `project
Id` is positional only, for REST consistency with sibling routes \\u2014 this endpoint authorizes per-suite, not per-project, so a

ny `projectId` returns the same disclosure for a `suiteId` you can reach.",
